cells.tense: You're here, tending it, and the tending is yours.
cells.verb: keeping what's growing between you and someone cared for without crowding it
cells.place: in the part of you that feels alongside people, not just about them
cells.ask: If you want it, let one person see what the tending has asked of you — not so they'll lift it, just so it's seen — and then let that piece be finished. What comes back is care that doesn't wear you out, and a hand that can hold without closing.
cells.core: You're keeping two things alive at once — what someone else needs and what you need — and you're doing it by paying attention, not by force. You can feel with people and still keep the shape of your own days. Nothing is being starved to feed the other. That's steadier than it looks from inside.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the care going without anyone going hungry for it.

cells.tense: You're already out ahead of this, bracing for a closeness that hasn't been asked for yet.
cells.verb: tending what grows between you and someone before it's had the chance to grow
cells.place: in the part of you that feels what another person feels
cells.ask: Let one thing that's already between you be enough for a day — sit in what's actually grown here before you plan its next feeding. What comes back is care that doesn't exhaust, and room for the other person to arrive on their own.
cells.core: You're managing the bond before it's had a chance to be one. You can feel what they might need next week, and you're already arranging for it — watering, pruning, checking — so the connection becomes something you run rather than something you're in. The person on the other side can feel the care. They can also feel the grip.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing the closeness instead of being in it.

cells.tense: You've stepped back from this, and you're still standing where you stepped back from.
cells.verb: letting what grows between you and someone go untended
cells.place: in the part of you that feels alongside people
cells.ask: Don't try to feel closer by effort. Instead, name one thing about being close to someone that you still want, right now, and keep wanting it on purpose for a week. What comes back is a hand that can hold space without clutching, because it isn't bracing for the weight.
cells.core: The tending has gone quiet, and the feeling-with has gone quiet with it. You still notice people. You just don't lean in to keep anything alive between you — the tools are down and your attention is elsewhere. What's missing isn't the ability to care. It's the reach toward it, which has gone slack.
cells.sheetLine: You've stepped back from tending it, and the closeness went quiet with you.

cells.tense: You're already doing this; you just haven't signed it.
cells.verb: tending what grows between you and someone, carefully, with both of you in mind
cells.place: in the part of you that feels what another person feels
cells.ask: Say it plainly to one person, once: that you've been looking after this between you, and that it was on purpose. What comes back is care that doesn't exhaust, because it finally has an owner.
cells.core: You're the one keeping this connection alive — remembering, adjusting, making room for what they need and quietly protecting what you need too — and you'd describe it as just how things are. The care is deliberate and it's working. The only person not giving you credit for it is you.
cells.sheetLine: You've been tending this all along. You call it nothing.

flags.detail: "you stopped believing" — a cell knows no one's past
